action: 1984 customers: watch the company's own channels for restoration; the company says email and DNS come back first, then other services once it is satisfied that customer data and systems are secure.
date_note: 1984's statement was published on 20 November, the day the shutdown began.
exec: An Icelandic hosting provider took its services offline after an attack it calls well-planned and technically advanced, and says it cannot yet say when all services will be normal.
geo_basis: country (company location not stated in the source)
plain: Icelandic web host 1984 shut down its services on 20 November after what its statement calls a well-organized and technically advanced attack. Reports differ on data theft: Xakep.ru says it happened, Iceland Review says it is unconfirmed.

sources.name: DV: joint statement of 1984 ehf. and CERT-IS, 20 Nov 2026

summary: Icelandic web host 1984 shut down its services on 20 November after a cyberattack; its statement with CERT-IS says the attack appears well-organized and technically advanced, and that it cannot yet say when all services will be normal. Xakep.ru reports attackers stole part of its internal data and that CERT-IS's head said they clearly used AI; Iceland Review says investigators had not confirmed whether data were stolen.
title: Icelandic web host 1984 takes services offline after major cyberattack, managing director says

validation.note: 1984 ehf. and CERT-IS joint statement (DV, 20 Nov) is primary; Iceland Review (21 Nov, relaying RUV) and Xakep.ru (23 Nov) also read. Xakep's claims of AI use and data theft come from Xakep only (it relays Icelandic media pages that did not load for me). Reviewer: Iceland Review (21 Nov) says it was not confirmed whether data were stolen, contradicting Xakep; both attributed in the summary.
